groups.title: Admonitive meaning
groups.proposal: Make admonitive meaning an enforced positive warning distinction on the normal application path.
groups.writingJob: Treat the admonitive as a positive cautionary warning or advice, never as an inherently negative prohibition.
groups.readingJob: Keep source-language admonition meaning distinct from negative-looking English translations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses admonitive mood; the application supplies its positive warning force and blocks false prohibition readings.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Mood; do not add a positive-versus-negative admonitive control.

groups.title: Admonitive VNC formation
groups.proposal: Keep admonitive formation automatic, nonpast-only, and class-sensitive.
groups.writingJob: Build only nonpast admonitive VNCs from the perfective stem with the correct class-conditioned tense morph and number dyad.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader distinguish the perfective-based admonitive shape and understand why a standalone VNC has no translation value.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses mood, subject, and stem; the application enforces nonpast tense, perfective stem, class shape, and number realization.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Mood, Subject, and stem class; do not expose automatic h, zero, t-in, or t-ih as choices.

groups.title: Affirmative admonition sentences
groups.proposal: Make affirmative admonition a normal sentence transformation with enforced warning meaning.
groups.writingJob: Convert an affirmative assertion into an admonition with obligatory mā, optional nēn, participant-based role, and warning-sense output.
groups.readingJob: Guide direct, indirect, and self-directed warning readings without turning them into prohibitions or wishes.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses admonitive mood, participant, and optional strengthening; the application supplies mā, placement, role, and valid warning interpretation.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Mood, Subject, and Particles; nēn remains the existing particle choice and mā is an application obligation.

groups.title: Class A admonitions
groups.proposal: Connect Class A admonition forms to the shared admonitive system.
groups.writingJob: Build and interpret singular and plural Class A affirmative admonitions.
groups.readingJob: Use the Class A examples to recognize h and participant-number differences.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives Class A form; the user supplies the stem and participant.

groups.title: Class B admonitions
groups.proposal: Connect Class B admonition forms to the shared admonitive system.
groups.writingJob: Build and interpret singular and plural Class B affirmative admonitions.
groups.readingJob: Use the Class B examples to recognize zero tense and admonitive number shapes.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives Class B form; the user supplies the stem and participant.

groups.title: Class C admonitions
groups.proposal: Connect Class C admonition forms to the shared admonitive system.
groups.writingJob: Build and interpret singular and plural Class C affirmative admonitions.
groups.readingJob: Use the Class C examples to recognize the perfective stem and warning meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives Class C form; the user supplies the stem and participant.

groups.title: Class D and nonhuman admonitions
groups.proposal: Connect Class D and nonhuman admonitions to the shared system.
groups.writingJob: Build Class D admonitions and preserve appropriate warning or advice interpretation for human and nonhuman subjects.
groups.readingJob: Guide Class D forms and nonhuman indirect-admonition translations without converting advice into a wish.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives the form and participant applicability; the reader chooses an appropriate translation wording.

groups.title: Negative admonition sentences
groups.proposal: Keep Lesson 10 negative admonition distinct from Lesson 9 negative command.
groups.writingJob: Build a negative admonition with ah and obligatory mā nēn as a cancellation of warning, not as a prohibition.
groups.readingJob: Guide the counter-caution meaning: be sure to act or reject caution.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses negative admonition; the application supplies ah, mā nēn, and the reversed caution meaning.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Polarity, Mood, and Particles; do not add a separate negative-prefix selector.

groups.title: General VNC contrasts
groups.proposal: Expose genuine form contrasts without turning analysis into choices.
groups.writingJob: Preserve second-person x or xi and plural morphology as dependable contrasts among moods.
groups.readingJob: Use person and number to distinguish admonitive, optative, present, and preterit forms.
groups.decisionSplit: The application generates the contrasts; the reading guide explains them.

groups.title: Class A contrast paradigm
groups.proposal: Make every Class A contrast available from canonical forms.
groups.writingJob: Generate the full Class A contrast paradigm and preserve each distinct or ambiguous relation.
groups.readingJob: Guide h, glottal-stop, mā, person, and number contrasts in Class A.
groups.decisionSplit: The application generates the paradigm; the reader uses the cues.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the full paradigm; no new control.

groups.title: Class B contrast paradigm
groups.proposal: Make every Class B contrast available from canonical forms.
groups.writingJob: Generate the full Class B contrast paradigm and enforce mā and antecessive distinctions.
groups.readingJob: Guide identical singular forms through sentence particles and antecessive ō.
groups.decisionSplit: The application generates forms and restrictions; the reader uses context.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse full paradigm and existing particles.

groups.title: Class C contrast paradigm
groups.proposal: Make every Class C contrast available from canonical forms.
groups.writingJob: Generate the full Class C contrast paradigm and enforce glottal, mā, and antecessive distinctions.
groups.readingJob: Guide ambiguous unmarked glottal-stop spellings through context.
groups.decisionSplit: The application generates forms and restrictions; the reader uses context.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse full paradigm and existing particles.

groups.title: Class D contrast paradigm
groups.proposal: Make Class D contrast structure available without inventing a new choice.
groups.writingJob: Generate Class D contrast forms and preserve the glottal-stop and second-person distinctions.

groups.decisionSplit: The application generates the form; the reader uses spelling and context cues.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse full paradigm and existing person controls.
